open_obligations.what_is_open: Construct, from the recorded divisor cases of \(\mathsf{Core}_{G,e}\), a source-prime-preserving finite-branch elimination routine that returns the true coordinate minimal polynomial and all required nonzero exceptional-set circuits within \(n^{C(k+1)}\operatorname{poly}(\log(1/\delta))\) time and certificate length.
open_obligations.obstruction: The frozen quadratic-core lemma is extensional: it bounds the variables and degrees and asserts preservation of the queried projection, but it supplies neither a bounded-size prime-component presentation for every pole and zero-over-zero stratum nor an effective lifting identity that distinguishes that component from extraneous components of the case-split equations. A generic zero-dimensional slice or rational-univariate representation of their union can therefore add spurious queried values or omit genuine divisor branches. No frozen result bounds circuits for the component selection, incidence lifting, slice coverage, projective leading forms, or real-lifting boundary factors required in \(\mathcal Q_{G,e}\). Assuming such a routine would assume the theorem's algorithmic crux.
open_obligations.attempted: I extended the prior bounded-core and multiplication-matrix reduction by giving a complete Jacobian-rank decision and dominance certificate for the transcendental tag. For the finite tag I followed the coordinate-preserving slice route on every recorded divisor stratum, but the available generic rational-univariate specialization result begins only after the correct zero-dimensional component has been selected and therefore does not close source-prime component selection or its circuit-size analysis.
open_obligations.partial_result:
The transcendental tag can be completed independently of the unresolved elimination backend.  Write the algebraically independent source coordinates as
\[
\theta=(\lambda_D,\omega_B,\omega_{\mathrm{diag}})=(\theta_1,\ldots,\theta_N)
\]
and enumerate the distinct covariance generators of \(K_G\) as \(f_a=\phi_G(\sigma_{i_a j_a})\), \(1\leq a\leq s\).  Over \(L=\mathbb C(\theta)\), define
\[
J_0=\left(\frac{\partial f_a}{\partial\theta_b}\right)_{a,b},
\qquad
J_1=\begin{pmatrix}J_0\\
\left(\dfrac{\partial\lambda_e}{\partial\theta_b}\right)_b
\end{pmatrix}.
\]
For rational functions \(g_1,\ldots,g_u\in L\), one has
\[
\operatorname{rank}_L\left(\frac{\partial g_a}{\partial\theta_b}\right)_{a,b}
=\operatorname{trdeg}_{\mathbb C}\mathbb C(g_1,\ldots,g_u).
\]
Indeed, choose a transcendence basis \(v_1,\ldots,v_r\) of \(\mathbb C(g_1,\ldots,g_u)/\mathbb C\).  Since the characteristic is zero, differentiating the separable algebraic equations of the \(g_a\)'s over \(\mathbb C(v_1,\ldots,v_r)\) shows that the \(dg_a\)'s span the same \(L\)-subspace of the module of K\"ahler differentials \(\Omega^1_{L/\mathbb C}\) as the \(dv_i\)'s.  Extending the \(v_i\)'s to a transcendence basis of \(L/\mathbb C\) shows that the \(dv_i\)'s are \(L\)-linearly independent, proving the equality.  Applying it twice gives
\[
\operatorname{rank}_L J_1-\operatorname{rank}_L J_0
=\operatorname{trdeg}_{K_G}K_G(\lambda_e)
=\begin{cases}
0,&\lambda_e\text{ is algebraic over }K_G,\\
1,&\lambda_e\text{ is transcendental over }K_G.
\end{cases}
\]
This is an exact algebraicity test, not a local-identification inference.

Acyclicity implies \(\Lambda^n=0\) after topological ordering and hence
\[
(I_n-\Lambda)^{-1}=\sum_{j=0}^{n-1}\Lambda^j.
\]
Consequently every entry of \(J_0\) and \(J_1\) has a source-polynomial arithmetic circuit of size polynomial in \(n\).  A checkable rank transcript for either matrix consists of a nonsingular pivot block \(A\) and the block identity
\[
D-CA^{-1}B=0.
\]
Multiplication by \(\det(A)\) turns the latter into polynomial-circuit identities; \(\det(A)\neq0\) is witnessed by one nonzero exact evaluation, while the zero identities are tested after source substitution.  There are polynomially many such identities of polynomial degree.  Choosing the finite sampling set according to \(\mathrm{lem:schwartz\mbox{-}zippel\mbox{-}bound}\) and applying a union bound makes the total erroneous-identity probability at most \(\delta\), with polynomially many arithmetic operations and \(\operatorname{poly}(\log(1/\delta))\) random-bit and certificate overhead.  On the rank-increase branch, \(K_G[t]\to A_K\), \(t\mapsto\lambda_e\), is injective because \(A_K\) is integral with fraction field \(L\) by \(\mathrm{thm:incidence\mbox{-}localization}\).  Thus \(\operatorname{Spec}(A_K)\to\mathbb A^1_{K_G}\) is dominant and positive dimensional.  The two rank transcripts therefore instantiate \(\mathcal N_{G,e}\) and complete the transcendental output tag within the asserted complexity bound.

On the algebraic branch, the previously established \(\mathrm{lem:quadratic\mbox{-}core}\) reduces the problem to at most \(r\leq2k\) variables and degree-two equations.  Once a source-prime-preserving zero-dimensional slice of a divisor stratum is supplied, its quotient has degree at most \(2^r\leq2^{2k}\); multiplication by \(\lambda_e\) on that quotient and the first linear dependence among its powers compute the coordinate eliminant over \(K_G\).  The established \(\mathrm{thm:orientation\mbox{-}upper\mbox{-}bound}\) then bounds the true irreducible factor by \(2^{k+1}\).  This gives the claimed \(n^{O(k+1)}\) arithmetic bound conditional only on constructing and certifying the correct stratum and slice.  What is not supplied by any frozen premise is an effective presentation that distinguishes the component birational to the integral source incidence algebra from extraneous components introduced by the recorded divisor cases.  Applying a generic rational-univariate routine to the union does not repair this: it can add queried-coordinate values from an extraneous component, while discarding a divisor can lose a genuine zero-over-zero branch.  The same missing component-and-lifting construction is needed to produce, with bounded circuits, all nonzero pole, projective-leading-form, slice-coverage, incidence-lifting, and real-lifting factors in \(\mathcal Q_{G,e}\).  Thus the transcendental branch and the bounded multiplication-matrix step are proved, but the finite tag and its certificate-size guarantee remain open.

proofs.proof_tex:
Fix \(G\). Introduce real indeterminates \(s=(s_{ij}:i\leq j)\), \(z\), and \(\ell=(\ell_f:f\in D)\). With \(F_{ij}(\ell,s)\) denoting the polynomial obtained from the displayed residual \(F_{ij}(\Lambda,\Sigma)\) by substitution, consider the first-order formula over ordered fields
\[
 \Phi_G(s,z)\;:\Longleftrightarrow\;
 \exists\ell\in\mathbb R^D\quad
 \left(\ell_e=z\right)\ \wedge\!
 \bigwedge_{\substack{i<j\\ i\leftrightarrow j\notin B}}
 \left(F_{ij}(\ell,s)=0\right).
\]
Every polynomial occurring here has rational coefficients: this follows directly from the definition of \(F_{ij}\), because \(G\), \(D\), and \(B\) only select variables and equations. By \(\mathrm{def:real\mbox{-}retained\mbox{-}set}\), for every real \((\Sigma,z)\),
\[
 \Phi_G(\Sigma,z)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 z\in\mathcal R_e(G,\Sigma).                                      \tag{1}
\]

Apply \(\mathrm{lem:effective\mbox{-}real\mbox{-}quantifier\mbox{-}elimination}\) to \(\Phi_G\), with \((s,z)\) as the free variables and \(\ell\) as the quantified block. It produces finitely many polynomials \(g_{ab}\in\mathbb Q[s,z]\) and signs \(\epsilon_{ab}\in\{-1,0,1\}\) such that the quantifier-free formula
\[
 \Psi_G(s,z)=
 \bigvee_a\bigwedge_b
 \left(\operatorname{sign}g_{ab}(s,z)=\epsilon_{ab}\right)          \tag{2}
\]
is equivalent to \(\Phi_G(s,z)\) over every real closed field, in particular over \(\mathbb R\). Combining (1) and (2) proves, for all real \((\Sigma,z)\),
\[
 \Psi_G(\Sigma,z)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 z\in\mathcal R_e(G,\Sigma).                                      \tag{3}
\]
This is the promised computable side of the characterization. Notice that (2) was obtained from the original polynomial residual equations. It contains neither a division nor a restriction to a zero-dimensional component, so (3) also covers positive-dimensional fibers and components lying entirely on a pole or denominator-zero locus introduced by any intermediate reduction.

Now let \(\Sigma\succ0\) be in the covariance-model image and outside \(\mathcal E_{G,e}\). By \(\mathrm{thm:exceptional\mbox{-}set\mbox{-}validity}\),
\[
 \{z\in\mathbb C:p_e(\Sigma,z)=0\}=\mathcal Z_e(G,\Sigma),          \tag{4}
\]
and the nonvanishing squarefreeness factor makes these roots distinct. Thus each real root in (4) is a genuine complex queried-coordinate value, while (3), rather than complex degree or local rank, decides whether that particular value has a real supported extension.

Suppose next that every entry of \(\Sigma\) is supplied by an exact real-algebraic representation. Evaluation of the rational arithmetic circuits for \(p_e\) is exact because all their certificate denominators are nonzero outside \(\mathcal E_{G,e}\). After clearing the resulting nonzero algebraic denominator, apply \(\mathrm{lem:real\mbox{-}algebraic\mbox{-}sampling}\) to the univariate zero set of the numerator. Because the polynomial is squarefree, its real zero set is finite and every point is a semialgebraically connected component. The output therefore enumerates every real root by a real univariate representation and Thom data; duplicate representations, if any, are removed by exact sign comparison. Rational isolating intervals are obtained by enumerating rational endpoint pairs and retaining the first disjoint pairs consistent with the finite ordered Thom list. Termination follows from finiteness of the root set and density of \(\mathbb Q\) in \(\mathbb R\).

For one enumerated root \(z\), all signs in (2) can be evaluated exactly in the real algebraic field generated by \(\Sigma\) and \(z\). If \(\Psi_G(\Sigma,z)\) is false, the evaluated sign list is a finite rejecting certificate by (3). If it is true, form
\[
 Q_{\Sigma,z}(\ell)
 = (\ell_e-z)^2+
   \sum_{\substack{i<j\\i\leftrightarrow j\notin B}}
   F_{ij}(\ell,\Sigma)^2.                                         \tag{5}
\]
Because the ambient field is ordered, a real vector \(\ell\) satisfies \(Q_{\Sigma,z}(\ell)=0\) if and only if every summand in (5) vanishes. Hence
\[
 Z_{\mathbb R}(Q_{\Sigma,z})\ne\varnothing
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \Phi_G(\Sigma,z)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 z\in\mathcal R_e(G,\Sigma).                                     \tag{6}
\]
The sampling lemma applied to (5) returns a real univariate representation of a point on every real connected component of this zero set, whatever its dimension. In the accepting case, choose any returned point; together with the root's isolating interval and the exact sign data from (2), it is \(\mathsf{LiftCert}\). Conversely, every point represented by an accepting certificate satisfies all equations in (5), and therefore is a complete real lift with queried coordinate \(z\). This proves the certificate's if-and-only-if property.

For completeness, the algebraic coefficient tower can be flattened into the stipulated rational-univariate format. If \(a\) and \(b\) are algebraic over \(\mathbb Q\), then among the finitely many pairs of distinct conjugate pairs \((a_i,b_j)\ne(a_{i'},b_{j'})\), equality \(a_i+c b_j=a_{i'}+c b_{j'}\) excludes at most one rational \(c\), unless \(b_j=b_{j'}\), in which case distinctness already forces \(a_i\ne a_{i'}\). Thus all but finitely many \(c\in\mathbb Q\) separate the conjugate pairs, and \(\mathbb Q(a,b)=\mathbb Q(a+cb)\). Iteration gives one primitive real algebraic element for the entries of \(\Sigma\), the root, and the sampled lift coordinates. Exact sign comparisons select its real conjugate and provide isolating data. Therefore every object in the certificate has a finite rational-univariate encoding.

It remains to verify the support and positivity conclusion. Put \(R=I_n-\Lambda\) for an accepted real lift. By \(\mathrm{ass:acyclic}\), a topological ordering makes \(\Lambda\) strictly triangular, so \(\Lambda\) is nilpotent and \(R\) is invertible. Define
\[
 \Omega=R^{\mathsf T}\Sigma R.
\]
For \(x\ne0\), invertibility gives \(Rx\ne0\), and positive definiteness of \(\Sigma\) gives
\[
 x^{\mathsf T}\Omega x
 =x^{\mathsf T}R^{\mathsf T}\Sigma Rx
 =(Rx)^{\mathsf T}\Sigma(Rx)>0.                                  \tag{7}
\]
Thus \(\Omega\succ0\). Direct multiplication, using the support of \(\Lambda\), yields for every \(i\ne j\)
\[
 \Omega_{ij}
 =\sigma_{ij}
 -\sum_{p\in\operatorname{pa}_D(i)}\lambda_{pi}\sigma_{pj}
 -\sum_{q\in\operatorname{pa}_D(j)}\lambda_{qj}\sigma_{iq}
 +\sum_{p\in\operatorname{pa}_D(i)}
       \sum_{q\in\operatorname{pa}_D(j)}
       \lambda_{pi}\lambda_{qj}\sigma_{pq}
 =F_{ij}(\Lambda,\Sigma).                                        \tag{8}
\]
The accepting equations make (8) zero whenever \(i\leftrightarrow j\notin B\), exactly the support restriction in \(\mathrm{ass:noise\mbox{-}support}\). Equations (7)--(8) show that every accepted lift gives a positive-definite supported disturbance covariance. Together with (3)--(6), this completes the corrected theorem without inferring real uniqueness from the complex degree.

added_lemmas.statement: Let \(R\) be a real closed field, let \(D_0\subseteq R\) be an ordered coefficient domain, and let \(\Phi(Y)\) be a first-order formula in the language of ordered fields whose atoms use finitely many polynomials in \(D_0[X,Y]\). There is an exact algorithm, using arithmetic and sign determination in \(D_0\), which produces a quantifier-free Boolean combination of polynomial sign conditions in the free variables \(Y\) that is equivalent to \(\Phi(Y)\) over \(R\).

source.verbatim_statement: In this paper, a new algorithm for performing quantifier elimination from first order formulas over real closed fields is given.

attestation.note: Transcribed from the abstract and matched to Theorem 1.3.1 of the published Journal of the ACM article.

added_lemmas.statement: Let \(R\) be a real closed field, let \(D_0\subseteq R\) be an ordered domain, let \(Q\in D_0[X_1,\ldots,X_s]\), and let \(\mathcal P\subset D_0[X_1,\ldots,X_s]\) be finite. There is an exact algebraic-sampling algorithm whose output consists of finitely many real univariate representations whose associated points meet every semialgebraically connected component of every nonempty realizable sign condition of \(\mathcal P\) on \(\{x\in R^s:Q(x)=0\}\).

proposed_statement_changes.proposed: Assume \(d_e(G)<\infty\). There is an effectively computable finite quantifier-free Boolean combination of polynomial sign conditions with rational coefficients in \((\Sigma,z)\) which, for every real \(\Sigma\succ0\) in the covariance-model image and outside \(\mathcal E_{G,e}\) and every simple real root \(z\) of \(p_e(\Sigma,\cdot)\), holds if and only if \(z\in\mathcal R_e(G,\Sigma)\). Thus it characterizes exactly which such roots extend to complete real supported directed coefficients. If the entries of \(\Sigma\) are real algebraic numbers supplied by exact univariate representations and isolating data, an exact post-specialization procedure enumerates the simple real roots and returns a finite \(\mathsf{LiftCert}\) for each root; the certificate accepts if and only if that root belongs to \(\mathcal R_e(G,\Sigma)\). The procedure uses the original residual equations, and therefore remains valid for positive-dimensional \(\Lambda\)-fibers and for real components contained in denominator-zero loci of intermediate reductions. For every accepted complete real supported \(\Lambda\), the recovered matrix \(\Omega=(I_n-\Lambda)^{\mathsf T}\Sigma(I_n-\Lambda)\) is positive definite by congruence. No finite exact evaluation claim is made for a specialization whose real entries have no supplied finite exact representation.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The original per-specialization algorithmic claim is not well typed for an arbitrary real covariance: the frozen exact arithmetic model supplies no finite encoding or sign oracle for arbitrary real entries, and the signature of the graph-level symbolic algorithm does not take such a specialization as input. The corrected claim keeps an exact semialgebraic membership characterization throughout the stated regular covariance domain, while restricting finite returned certificates to real-algebraic specializations with supplied exact encodings. It also makes the post-specialization procedure explicit and tests the original residual fiber, including positive-dimensional and pole-divisor components.

proposed.justification: Complex degree is not a real ambiguity count, so root-by-root extension is required before a causal coefficient value is reported.
proposed.gap: Drton, Foygel, and Sullivant separate real positive-definite fibers from complex genericity, and Bouzidi et al. isolate real solutions; the missing result is an if-and-only-if supported-SEM lift for each projected coordinate root.
proposed.consumer: Applied SEM analysts receive all and only real structural explanations of a regular observed covariance, without a false uniqueness conclusion from local rank.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The narrowed claim uses two classical real-algebraic algorithms and acyclicity directly; this replacement declares those proof dependencies and removes the graph-level symbolic algorithm from the claim's free-symbol set.
